channel.title: Security on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in Security on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: security: Post-quantum authentication: Why organizations should start testing certificate ecosystems now
item.description:
Microsoft says organizations should begin testing certificate ecosystems now to prepare for post-quantum authentication. The post highlights Microsoft’s PQC TLS Pilot Program as a way to validate readiness for future post-quantum TLS deployments.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: 3 lessons from frontier AI vulnerability research
item.description:
Microsoft Security says its FORGE Lab is applying frontier AI methods to scale vulnerability research beyond Windows, including work on the Linux kernel. The post highlights three takeaways from that research effort.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: CISO perspectives on managing vulnerability risks in the age of AI
item.description:
The post says CISOs should adapt vulnerability management practices for AI-driven environments to reduce cybersecurity risk and improve resilience. It frames the topic as managing vulnerabilities in the age of AI-powered tooling and threats.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Insights from the 2026 Microsoft Digital Defense Report
item.description:
Microsoft published a brief post pointing readers to highlights from the 2026 Microsoft Digital Defense Report. The note says the security environment is becoming more interconnected, but provides no detailed findings in the excerpt.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Preparing governments for an era of interconnected cyber risk
item.description:
Microsoft says government agencies and services were the most impacted sector in 2026 cyber activity, accounting for 27% of observed activity versus 17% in 2025. The post ties this to Microsoft’s 2026 Digital Defense Report and frames it as interconnected cyber risk for governments.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: ​​Secure what’s next: Your guide to Microsoft Security at Microsoft Ignite 2026
item.description:
Microsoft’s Ignite 2026 security post says the company will highlight an AI-first, end-to-end security platform. The platform is described as covering identities, devices, data, applications, clouds, infrastructure, and AI agents.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Unauthenticated command injection on internet-facing mail servers: tracking CVE-2026-73570
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports active exploitation of CVE-2026-73570 in Zimbra mail servers. The post covers observed attack paths, ways to detect the activity, and mitigation guidance.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Phishing Abuses RMM Tools for Persistent Access
item.description:
Microsoft reported phishing campaigns that abused MSP360 RMM to deploy ScreenConnect and establish redundant remote-access channels for later malicious activity. The focus is on persistence and follow-on access rather than initial compromise alone.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: ​​Beyond source code: A path to the keys to the kingdom
item.description:
Microsoft describes how Storm-3068 used a compromised identity to expand access into cloud environments, moving beyond source code exposure to broader infrastructure compromise. The post focuses on defensive steps for protecting identities, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud infrastructure.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Star Blizzard refines phishing and malware delivery with the RedFlick technique
item.description:
Microsoft says it has observed Russian state actor Star Blizzard since January 2026 using large-scale phishing, compromised website accounts, and a new malware delivery method it tracks as RedFlick. The update focuses on the actor’s improved detection evasion and delivery techniques.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: NeedyMantis: Unpacking a post-compromise malware family used in targeted operations
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence identified NeedyMantis, a modular post-compromise malware framework used in targeted intrusions. It uses custom loaders, encrypted archives, and extensible components to keep access and support follow-on activity.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Storm-3168: Agentic-driven cloud attacks using compromised service principals
item.description:
Microsoft describes Azure attacks linked to Storm-3168 using compromised service principals, including reconnaissance, resource deletion, and credential access. The post links the activity to JADEPUFFER and includes defender guidance.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Beyond the ransomware: Tracking Storm-2570’s consistent tradecraft across deployments
item.description:
Microsoft says Storm-2570 reuses the same post-compromise tools and techniques across multiple ransomware deployments, including Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis, and BERT. The post outlines guidance for defenders to detect and disrupt the activity before ransomware is deployed.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: ​​​​​​​​What’s new in Microsoft Security: September 2026​​
item.description:
Microsoft Security’s September 2026 update focuses on discovering and controlling local AI agents, extending Zero Trust controls to agent traffic, and improving SOC foundational capabilities.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Reimagining the SOC for the agentic era in Microsoft Defender
item.description:
Microsoft announced ISOC in Microsoft Defender, a foundation for agentic security that combines SIEM and threat protection capabilities in one place. The post positions this as part of reworking the SOC for agentic-era operations.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Unmasking EvilTokens: Getting to the root of device code phishing
item.description:
Microsoft says EvilTokens emerged as a major phishing-as-a-service platform for device code phishing, using AI-assisted lures, automated infrastructure, and token theft. In collaboration with partners, Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit disrupted its infrastructure and operations.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: From guidance to action: Security fundamentals that materially reduce risk
item.description:
Microsoft says AI has changed the cybersecurity operating environment and points readers to exposure management guidance with recommended controls. The post emphasizes taking action on security fundamentals to reduce risk.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Improving email security outcomes with real-world Microsoft Defender insights
item.description:
Microsoft says its latest email security benchmarking reports show strong Defender performance in both pre-delivery and post-delivery scenarios. The post also notes ongoing changes in how threats and defenses are evolving.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Protecting organizations from AI-assisted executive impersonation and invoice fraud
item.description:
Microsoft describes an AI-assisted business email compromise campaign that impersonated executives and used fake invoices to target finance teams for ACH payment fraud. The post focuses on the attack pattern and how organizations can protect against it.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Detect and disrupt AI-themed attacks with Microsoft Defender
item.description:
Microsoft Defender is described as detecting and disrupting AI-themed phishing, malware, and multi-stage attacks across the attack chain. The post is a Microsoft Security Blog entry dated 2026-09-10.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Threat matrix: Mapping threats across cloud web applications
item.description:
Microsoft introduced the Cloud Web Applications Threat Matrix, a MITRE ATT&CK-aligned framework for understanding and prioritizing threats against cloud-hosted web applications and serverless platforms. It is intended to help defenders map attacks and identify mitigations.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Passkey-themed social engineering leads to identity and cloud compromise
item.description:
Microsoft describes a threat campaign using passkey-themed social engineering to compromise identities and extend access into cloud services. The activity includes MFA persistence, Microsoft Graph reconnaissance, and access to SharePoint, OneDrive, and email data, with guidance on detection and mitigation.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: How to secure edge AI in customer-owned environments
item.description:
Microsoft says edge AI deployments in customer-owned environments require stronger verification of systems, software, and AI assets before sharing sensitive data, credentials, or models. The post frames secure edge AI as a trust and validation problem for third-party environments.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: ASCII smuggling crosses over from AI prompt injection to phishing evasion
item.description:
Microsoft reports that invisible Unicode characters, previously used in AI prompt injection, are now being used to hide words from email filters as part of phishing evasion. The technique relies on obfuscating text before parsers process it.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Impersonating IT support: how threat actors turn a remote session into enterprise-wide access
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported a human-operated intrusion campaign that abuses Microsoft Teams external collaboration to impersonate IT support, gain remote access, and deploy a Node.js-based implant. The campaign uses social engineering and legitimate tools to move from initial access to lateral movement, with Microsoft Defender used for detection and disruption.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Counterfeit installers to system compromise: Tracking a deceptive software download campaign
item.description:
Microsoft describes an active malware campaign that uses fake software download pages and repackaged installer archives to impersonate legitimate vendors. The post includes observed tactics, Defender XDR detections, indicators of compromise, and mitigation guidance.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Cybersecurity IR Workshop: The workshop you shouldn’t miss
item.description:
Microsoft Security blog post promoting a cybersecurity incident response workshop focused on preparedness and response. It says the workshop shares practical insights from DART to improve cyber resilience before a crisis.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: TerminalFix campaign deploys a reverse tunnel through multistage intrusion
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence analyzed the TerminalFix ClickFix campaign, which uses fake CAPTCHA prompts, DLL sideloading, and a reverse tunnel in a multistage intrusion. The post includes detections and hunting guidance.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: ​​​​​​What’s new in Microsoft Security: August 2026
item.description:
Microsoft’s August 2026 security update highlights new capabilities for monitoring agent activity, broader security coverage across supported environments, and improved security management across environments.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: When AI infrastructure becomes the target: Securing gateways and control points
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports on attacks against exposed AI infrastructure, focusing on LiteLLM gateway exploitation and related credential theft, persistence, and cryptomining activity. The post highlights gateways and other control points as targets that need protection.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: The patch window is collapsing: Why security needs a new control plane
item.description:
Microsoft Security says organizations need protection that works between vulnerability discovery and remediation, because the patch window is shrinking. The post argues for a new security control plane to cover that gap.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Microsoft named a Leader in the Frost Radar™: Cloud Workload Protection Platforms, 2026
item.description:
Microsoft says it was named a visionary leader in Frost & Sullivan’s 2026 Frost Radar for Cloud Workload Protection Platforms, citing Microsoft Defender for Cloud’s unified runtime security. The post is a brief recognition announcement with no product changes described.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Hunting MacSync Stealer infrastructure through behavioral pivots
item.description:
Microsoft describes how it tracked MacSync Stealer infrastructure despite rapid domain rotation by using stable behavioral pivots. The investigation identified more than 30 related domains.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Microsoft named a Leader in the 2026 IDC MarketScape for MDR/MXDR for the Enterprise
item.description:
Microsoft says it was named a Leader in the 2026 IDC MarketScape for MDR/MXDR for the Enterprise. The post highlights Microsoft Defender Experts MDR as combining AI, threat intelligence, and human expertise.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: DeadLock ransomware: Breaking down a Rust-based encryptor with decentralized recovery infrastructure
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes DeadLock ransomware as a financially motivated operation using a Rust-based encryptor and decentralized infrastructure for victim communications, negotiations, and data leak operations. The group uses double extortion to pressure victims.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: ​​Microsoft named a Leader in the KuppingerCole Leadership Compass for Cloud Native Application Protection Platforms (CNAPP)
item.description:
Microsoft says KuppingerCole named it a Leader in the Leadership Compass for Cloud Native Application Protection Platforms (CNAPP). The provided excerpt does not include technical changes or product updates beyond that recognition.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: From open lures to cloaked gates: How a macOS ClickFix campaign learned to hide
item.description:
Microsoft describes a macOS ClickFix campaign that changed from openly delivering infostealer lures to placing them behind a browser-fingerprinting gate. The shift reduces visibility of the malicious infrastructure but also creates new detection opportunities for defenders.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: ChainDrop supply chain compromise: Anatomy of a self-propagating worm
item.description:
Microsoft describes ChainDrop, a credential-stealing worm embedded in 400+ compromised npm packages that spread by republishing malicious updates across software ecosystems. The post outlines the attack chain, affected environments, and guidance for detection, hunting, and remediation.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Advance Zero Trust for AI: New tools and guidance to secure AI agents and DevSecOps
item.description:
Microsoft says it is expanding its Zero Trust for AI strategy with new tools and guidance aimed at securing AI agents and DevSecOps environments. The post highlights a broader security approach for AI and related development workflows.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: 128 Seconds to disruption: Microsoft Defender stops ransomware at QNET
item.description:
Microsoft Defender isolated a compromised QNET endpoint in 128 seconds, interrupting a multi-stage ransomware attack before the payload could persist or spread.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: CaptiveCrunch: Midnight Blizzard targets travelers worldwide for malware delivery and credential theft
item.description:
Microsoft says Storm-2945, a sub-cluster of Midnight Blizzard, has been compromising sign-in portals at hospitality organizations since May 2026 to deliver malware to travelers and steal credentials. The campaign is named CaptiveCrunch and targets travelers worldwide.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: ​​​​What’s new in Microsoft Security: July 2026
item.description:
Microsoft’s July 2026 Security update highlights new capabilities for securing AI environments, using AI for defense, and improving the underlying systems that AI-powered operations rely on. The provided excerpt does not include specific product changes or feature details.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: ​​Better security starts with better questions
item.description:
Microsoft Security says stronger security decisions come from asking better questions, using trusted AI, and combining AI outputs with human judgment. The post frames this as a way to help leaders make more confident decisions and build more resilient systems.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Rethinking security for the age of AI
item.description:
Microsoft says cybersecurity is changing in the AI era and introduces a new security cyber stack called Project Perception. The post frames this as a rethink of security architecture rather than a specific product release.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Enhancing AI security through global AI red teaming
item.description:
Microsoft announced EXTRA, a global AI security initiative focused on AI safety research and red teaming. The program partners with universities, researchers, and regional experts to identify emerging AI risks and improve testing of frontier AI systems.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Email threat landscape: Q2 2026 trends and insights
item.description:
Microsoft reports that Q2 2026 saw continued declines in several phishing techniques after disruption of the Tycoon2FA platform. Attackers shifted toward Teams-based social engineering and more automated, multi-stage attack chains.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Real world incident response: Microsoft and AXA XL strengthen cyber resilience
item.description:
Microsoft and AXA XL are collaborating to give cyber insurance policyholders direct access to Microsoft Incident Response services. The goal is to help organizations coordinate technical response, business decisions, and insurance actions during incidents.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Microsoft at Black Hat USA 2026: Defending trust in the age of AI and supply chain attacks
item.description:
Microsoft Security says it will be at Black Hat USA 2026 with sessions on supply chain research, hands-on security experiences, expert conversations, and a reception. The post frames the event around trust, AI, and supply chain attacks.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: ACR Stealer: Two observed intrusion chains amid increased threat activity
item.description:
Microsoft Defender Experts observed increased ACR Stealer activity from late April to mid-June 2026 across customer environments. The campaigns used ClickFix lures to steal browser credentials, authentication tokens, and sensitive documents from enterprise environments.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Least privilege for AI agents: Identity, access, and tool binding
item.description:
Microsoft Security published a post on applying least-privilege principles to AI agents, focusing on identity, access control, tool binding, and auditing as agents become more autonomous.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Unpacking the AsyncAPI npm supply chain compromise and import-time payload delivery
item.description:
Microsoft reports that attackers compromised AsyncAPI npm packages and used trusted CI/CD workflows to distribute malware via npm. The writeup details the attack chain, import-time payload delivery, and suggested defenses.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Turning threat intelligence into decisive action with Defender Experts
item.description:
Microsoft Security describes a Defender Experts post about helping security teams turn threat intelligence into action across endpoints, identities, cloud workloads, and third-party tools. The excerpt emphasizes that teams have more visibility but still face uncertainty from fragmented signals.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Defending SaaS-based applications against ShinyHunters OAuth abuse
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported ShinyHunters-linked activity targeting SaaS-based applications through OAuth abuse, vishing, supply-chain compromise, and misconfigured guest access. The post focuses on how these techniques were used against SaaS environments and how to defend against them.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Microsoft Entra ID security updates: Passkeys are the default authentication method in Entra ID
item.description:
Microsoft Entra ID now uses passkeys as the default sign-in method and introduces a new authentication model for SMS and voice. The post also points users to preparation guidance for the change.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Securing our future: July 2026 progress report on Microsoft’s Secure Future Initiative
item.description:
Microsoft published its July 2026 Secure Future Initiative progress report, summarizing work on secure foundations, AI-assisted defense, and broader cybersecurity readiness. The provided text is only a brief overview and does not include specific implementation details or metrics.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog
